title: Day-One Post-Op Review

patient.name: Mdm Nair Saraswathy
patient.presenting_complaint: Day 1 post-op review after right eye cataract surgery yesterday

history.hpc: Mdm Nair had right eye phacoemulsification and IOL implantation yesterday afternoon. She is here for her day-1 review. She says the eye feels a bit gritty but there is no severe pain. She can see some improvement in vision compared to before surgery. She had watery discharge from the eye overnight. She slept with the eye shield on as instructed.
history.pmhx: Hypertension, right eye cataract (now operated). No known allergies.
medications: Prednisolone acetate 1% eye drops — 4 times a day right eye (post-op)
Tobramycin 0.3% eye drops — 4 times a day right eye (post-op)
Nepafenac 0.1% eye drops — 3 times a day right eye (post-op)
history.social_hx: Came with husband. Does not drive.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Right eye: clear cornea, well-centred IOL in posterior chamber, anterior chamber formed. Mild conjunctival redness (expected post-op). Wound appears intact. No purulent discharge. Left eye: normal.
examination_findings.fundus: Not assessed today — routine day-1 review

investigations.va_distance: RE: LogMAR 0.3 (6/12). Improvement from pre-op baseline (6/60).
investigations.iop_nct: RE: 16 mmHg. LE: 14 mmHg. Within normal limits post-operatively.
investigations.wound_assessment: Wound clean and intact. No leakage noted. No signs of infection.

diagnosis: Day 1 post-cataract surgery — right eye. Normal post-operative findings. VA improved. No signs of complication (no severe pain, no significant discharge, no hypopyon, wound intact, IOP normal).

immediate: Remove old eye dressing carefully using sterile technique
Observe and document wound appearance, redness, discharge
Measure and record VA and IOP
Apply clean eye dressing if required or advise on eye hygiene
Document all findings and hand over to doctor
Reinforce post-operative drop regimen and technique
follow_up: Doctor to review wound and anterior segment
Advise patient on activity restrictions (no rubbing, no water in eye, no heavy lifting)
Next review appointment to be given
patient_education: Remind patient to continue all three post-op eye drops as scheduled
No rubbing of the operated eye
Avoid getting water in the eye when bathing — use a clean flannel
Wear eye shield at night for 1 week
Return immediately if: severe pain, sudden vision loss, increased redness or discharge

key_points: Asks about pain level (gritty/mild expected; severe pain is a red flag)
Asks about vision change since surgery (should be improved)
Asks about type and amount of discharge (watery normal; yellow/green/purulent is concerning)
Confirms patient wore eye shield overnight as instructed
Measures VA in operated eye (compare to pre-op baseline)
Measures IOP in operated eye (post-op IOP spike is a concern)
Observes and documents wound appearance (intact, clean, no leakage)
Identifies normal post-operative findings (mild gritty feeling, watery discharge, mild redness — all expected)
Recognises red flags that are absent: no severe pain, no purulent discharge, no wound leak, IOP normal
Confirms VA has improved from baseline (good surgical outcome)
Does not diagnose complication where none exists
Uses sterile technique for dressing change
Educates patient on post-op drop regimen (frequency, technique, correct eye)
Gives clear instructions on activity restrictions
Tells patient warning signs to watch for and when to return urgently
